column1: Now let’s return to the first question—what is the welfare cost of inflation? Beginning with Bailey (1956), this welfare cost has been calculated from the area under the money demand curve (showing money demand as a function of the nominal rate of interest) because this provides a measure of the consumer surplus lost as a result of having a positive nominal rate of interest.
